full_judgment:
By this application under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure, the pre-emptor-petitioner calls in question the propriety of an order dated February 22, 1993 passed in a pre-emption proceeding under section 96 of State Acquisition and Tenancy Act accepting the report of the Commissioner whereupon a Rule was issued calling upon the opposite-party Nos. 1 and 2 to show cause as to why the order dated 22-2-1993 passed by the learned Assistant Judge, Chuadanga in Miscellaneous Case No. 23 of 1983 should not be set aside. 

 2. Shorn of the avoidable details the material facts necessary for the disposal of the Rule are that, the pre-emptor-petitioner in the capacity of a co-sharer by inheritance of the holding of ''Ka'' schedule land and co-sharer by purchase of ''Kha'' schedule land filed an application being numbered as Miscellaneous Case No. 23 of 1983 in the Court of learned Munsif, Chuadanga under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act for pre-empting the land described in the schedule. The pre-emptee-opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 contested the suit by presenting written objection taking the stand that after purchase, he developed the land and constructed godown and incurred a total expenditure of an amount of Taka 35,000.00. 

 30. Record of the case was called for at the time of issuance of the Rule. On a close scrutiny and examination of the order-sheet and materials on record, it transpires that the court did not direct the parties to the suit to appear before the Engineer Commissioner on the date of Local investigation. It reveals, also, that the Engineer Commissioner did not at all issue any notice upon any of the parties to the suit. It is not known whether the Engineer Commissioner had sent any oral information to the pre-emptee-opposite-parties but it is manifestly clear that no notice was issued to the pre-emptor-petitioner. In the report submitted by the learned commissioner it is not at all stated that after issuing notice upon the parties he held the investigation. In the report he simply stated that he held the investigation and submitted the report. The learned commissioner was examined by the court in support of the report. In his evidence he categorically stated in the cross-examination that he did not issue any notice upon the parties. The relevant portion of his evidence in cross-examination is extracted below.
